<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" />{{rh|||381}}</noinclude>may, and geuing no offence to them that are weake. Thus he disputeth, and thus he exhorteth through the whole Epistle: though, if we wil diuide it by that which is principal in ech parte, vve may say, that vnto the 12 chapter is his disputation: and from thence to the end, his exhortation.

''Novv, in those points of faith, and in al others (as also in example of life) the commendation that he giueth to the Church of Rome,''{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Rom. 1.''}} ''is much to be noted.'' Your faith is renoumed in the vvhole vvorld. and your obediēce is published into euery place.{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Rom. 16.''}} I reioyce therfore in you. ''And againe:''{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Rom. 6.''}} you haue obeied from the hart vnto that forme of doctrine, vvhich hath been deliuered to you. ''And therevpon againe:'' I desire you brethren,{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Rom. 16.''}} to marke them that make dissensions and scandals contrarie to the doctrine vvhich you haue learned, and auoide them. For such doe not serue Christ our Lord, but theire ovvne belly: and by svveete speaches ad benedictions seduce the harts of innocents. ''Therfore'' to shunne Luther and Caluin, and al their crewes, vve haue iust reason and good vvarrant. They make dissensions and scandals against the doctrine of the Romane Church. Let no man therefore be seduced by their sugred vvordes.<noinclude>{{rh||Bbb iij|THE}}</noinclude>
